name: Freemasonry
notes: Many independent jurisdictions; rituals vary by jurisdiction and period.

name: Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn
notes: Original order fragmented after 1900; several modern successor orders claim the name.

name: Ordo Templi Orientis
notes: Several competing organizations use the name.

name: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
notes: Temple ceremonies are described by the church as sacred rather than secret.

name: Druze
notes: Divided into initiated (ʿuqqāl) and uninitiated (juhhāl) members.

name: Transcendental Meditation
notes: Presents itself as a non-religious technique; its religious status is disputed. In Malnak v. Yogi (1977–1979) US federal courts held that its school course was religious in nature.

name: Tibetan Buddhism (Vajrayana)
notes: Tantric practice is organised by lineages of the Nyingma, Kagyu, Sakya and Gelug schools.

name: Shingon Buddhism
notes: Main centres at Mount Kōya and Tō-ji.

name: Śākta Tantra (Kaula and Śrīvidyā)
notes: Goddess-centred tantric lineages; the Wikidata item is for Shaktism as a whole.

name: Naqshbandi order
notes: Sunni Sufi order with many branches, including the Mujaddidi and Khalidi lines.

name: Bektashi Order
notes: Banned in Turkey with all Sufi orders in 1925; the world headquarters moved to Tirana.

name: Eleusinian Mysteries
notes: Ended at the close of the 4th century CE.

name: Mithraic Mysteries
notes: No internal text explaining the cult survives.

name: Hopi religion
notes: Ceremonies are held by clans and religious societies in the Hopi villages. Wikidata has an item for the Hopi people (Q117255) but not for the religion.

name: Ngarrindjeri religion
region: Lower Murray and Coorong, South Australia
notes: Wikidata has an item for the Ngarrindjeri people (Q370543) but not for the religion.

name: Heaven and Earth Society (Tiandihui, Hung League)
founded: 18th century (its legend places the founding under the Kangxi emperor)
notes: Sworn brotherhood with initiation rites, oaths and recognition signs. Later Hung lodges and the triads claim descent from it.

name: Daoism
notes: Scriptures, talismans and methods were transmitted from master to disciple under covenant (CLM-0048, CLM-0049).

name: Alawites (Nusayris)
notes: The religion is taught to men through a staged initiation (CLM-0054).

name: Brahmanical (Vedic) tradition
notes: The tradition of Vedic recitation and the rites of the twice-born as laid down in the Dharmaśāstras.

name: Shugendō
notes: Mountain asceticism combining esoteric Buddhism with Japanese kami worship; major centres at Ōmine, Kumano and Haguro.
